eitc.title: Earned Income & Child Tax Credit Calculator
eitc.subtitle: Estimates Korea's earned income tax credit (EITC) and child tax credit for {a}–{b} income under the current law, following the official decree tables, including the property cut, late-filing cut, minimum payments and the child tax credit offset.

input.title: Household, income and assets

householdHint.single: No spouse, no dependent child under 18 and no supported parent aged 70+.
householdHint.one: Your spouse earns under ₩3,000,000, or you have no spouse but support a child under 18 or a parent aged 70+ (income ≤ ₩1,000,000, living with you).
householdHint.two: You and your spouse each earn ₩3,000,000 or more.

input.wageHint: Total salary on your withholding receipt, excluding tax-free pay. Include daily-work wages. Exclude pay received from parents, children or other lineal relatives.
input.businessHint: Freelance (3.3%), delivery or self-employed revenue. Only revenue × the industry adjustment rate counts. Exclude unregistered business income (withheld personal services still count) and real-estate rental income.

rates.etc: Mining, car & parts sales, other industries {p}%
rates.brokerage: Commodity brokerage, IT services, insurance & pensions {p}%
rates.finance: Finance, arts & leisure, repair & personal services {p}%
rates.professional: Real-estate services, professional & technical, business support, education, health & welfare {p}%
rates.personal: Personal services (freelance, delivery), non-property rental, household work {p}%

input.otherHint: Interest, dividends and pension income (gross), other income, and 90% of rental revenue. Used only to test the total-income limit; it does not change the credit amount.
input.propertyHint: Sum as of June 1 of the income year: homes, land and buildings (official standard value), cars, rental deposits, savings and stocks. Debts are not subtracted.
input.childrenHint: Annual income of ₩1,000,000 or less and under 18 at any time that year. No age limit for severe disability.
input.childrenSingle: A single household has no dependent children, so the child tax credit does not apply. A parent with children but no spouse counts as single-earner.
input.childCreditHint: The tax reduction you got from the child tax credit in year-end settlement or your tax return. It is subtracted from the child credit. Enter 0 if you had no tax to reduce.

methodHint.regular: File in May on the full year's income. Wages and business income both qualify.
methodHint.late: Filing within 6 months after the May window pays {p}% of the amount.
methodHint.half: With wages only, file for each half (September and March) and get {h}% of the annual amount in December.

result.disclaimer: This is an estimate. The National Tax Service decides the actual amount from payroll and asset records, and rounding may differ from the Hometax simulator. Exclusions such as nationality, licensed professionals and full-time workers averaging ₩5,000,000+ a month, and religious-worker income are not modeled.

text.flat: Earnings of {x} are on the plateau ({up}–{flat}), so you get the maximum {max}.
text.falling: Earnings of {x} are in the phase-out range ({flat}–{limit}). The credit drops about ₩{slope} for every ₩1,000,000 more income.

breakdown.ctcNone: No dependent children, or not eligible for the child credit.

limits.property: Assets {half}+ halve the credit; {cap}+ makes you ineligible (debts not subtracted).

pay.title: Filing and payment
pay.deferred: If the first-half amount is under ₩150,000, nothing is paid in December and it is all settled in June.
pay.regular: File May 1–31 (next business day if the last day is a holiday); payment by the end of September. In 2026 it was paid on August 27.
pay.late: File within 6 months after the May window (until December 1, 2026 for 2025 income); paid within 4 months of filing.
pay.half: File the first half on September 1–15 for December payment (December 17 planned in 2026) and the second half on March 1–15 next year for June settlement. The split assumes income evenly spread over the year. The child credit is decided with the May filing.

next.title: Changes may start with 2027 income
next.body: The government's 2026 tax reform plan (announced August 3, 2026, pending in the National Assembly) raises the income limits to ₩26M single, ₩37M single-earner and ₩52M dual-earner, the maximums to ₩1.8M, ₩3.1M and ₩3.6M, and widens the dual-earner plateau to ₩8M–₩18M. If passed it applies from 2027 income (September 2027 half-year filing). 2026 income (May 2027 filing) uses the rules in this calculator, and 2025 income can still be filed late (95%) until December 1, 2026.

calc.title: How the amount is set
items: The EITC has three ranges by earnings: phase-in, plateau and phase-out. Single households phase in below ₩4M, get the maximum ₩1.65M from ₩4M to ₩9M, and phase out from ₩9M to ₩22M.
Single-earner: phase-in below ₩7M, maximum ₩2.85M from ₩7M to ₩14M, phase-out to ₩32M. Dual-earner: phase-in below ₩8M, maximum ₩3.3M from ₩8M to ₩17M, phase-out to ₩44M.
Earnings = gross wages + business revenue × industry adjustment rate (20–90%) + religious-worker income, combined for the couple.

The actual amount comes from the decree's Appendix 11 table in ₩100k bands, not the raw formula. This calculator follows the table, so it can differ from the formula by about ₩40k. Below ₩4M the table never gives single-earners less than single households.
Amounts under ₩15,000 are not paid. In phase-in, ₩15,000–₩100,000 becomes ₩100,000; in phase-out, ₩15,000–₩30,000 becomes ₩30,000.

apply.title: When to file and get paid
items: May filing: May 1–31 of the following year (next business day if the last day is a holiday). Paid by the end of September; in 2026 it was paid on August 27.

Half-year filing: wage-only households file the first half on September 1–15 and the second half on March 1–15. 35% of the annual amount is paid in December and the rest is settled in June. Filing the first half counts as filing the second.
If the first-half amount is under ₩150,000 it is paid at the June settlement instead. Overpayments found at settlement may have to be returned.
Late filing: within 6 months after the May window, paying 95% within 4 months of filing.
How to file: the QR code on the NTS notice or the mobile notice, ARS 1544-9944, or Hometax (PC or mobile). Without a notice, file directly on Hometax. Help line: 1566-3636.
Consenting to automatic filing lets the NTS file for you in later years. Unpaid taxes can absorb up to 30% of the payment.

household.title: Household type
items: Single: no spouse, no dependent child under 18 and no supported parent aged 70+.
Single-earner: your spouse earns under ₩3,000,000, or you have no spouse but a dependent child or a parent aged 70+ (income ≤ ₩1,000,000, registered and living with you).
Dual-earner: you and your spouse each earn ₩3,000,000 or more, so combined earnings under ₩6,000,000 cannot be dual-earner.
Marital status is judged by the family register on December 31 of that year; half-year filing uses December 31 of the previous year.

Non-citizens cannot apply unless married to a Korean citizen or supporting a child with Korean nationality. People who are another person's dependent and licensed professionals (including spouses) are excluded.

property.title: Asset test
items: All household members' assets must total under ₩240M, and ₩170M or more halves the credit. Assets are measured on June 1 of the income year (June 1, 2025 for 2025 income).

Homes, land and buildings at official standard value, cars at standard value (business cars excluded), deposits, savings, insurance, stocks and bonds at balance, memberships, and rights to acquire property all count.

A rental deposit counts at the lower of the contract amount and the deemed deposit (55% of the home's standard price for 2025 income). Homes rented from lineal relatives count at 100% of the standard price.
Mortgages and deposit loans are not subtracted. A home bought with a loan counts at its full value.

child.title: Child tax credit
items: Single-earner and dual-earner households with dependent children under 18 qualify, with total income under ₩70M and assets under ₩240M, even above the EITC income limit.
Up to ₩1M per child. Single-earners get ₩1M below ₩21M of earnings and dual-earners below ₩25M; above that it falls to just over ₩500k per child near ₩70M.
You can apply even if you claimed the child tax credit at year-end; that credit is subtracted, and if less than ₩30,000 remains you get ₩30,000.
The 50% asset cut and the 95% late-filing rate apply just as for the EITC.

tips.title: Good to know
items: The total-income limit counts interest, dividends, pensions and other income too, but the credit amount uses earnings only.
The ₩44M dual-earner limit is combined. When marriage turns single households into a dual-earner one, the maximum and ranges change, so check the household comparison.
Daily workers who apply are treated as having filed an income tax return.
False claims must be repaid with penalty interest and bar you from the credit for 2 years (intent or gross negligence) or 5 years (fraud).

items.a: ₩1.65M for single, ₩2.85M for single-earner and ₩3.3M for dual-earner households, with total income under ₩22M, ₩32M and ₩44M respectively. The maximum applies at earnings of ₩4M–₩9M (single), ₩7M–₩14M (single-earner) and ₩8M–₩17M (dual-earner).

items.q: How are single-earner and dual-earner told apart?
items.a: If you and your spouse each earn ₩3,000,000 or more, you are dual-earner; if your spouse earns less, single-earner. Without a spouse, a dependent child under 18 or a parent aged 70+ (income ≤ ₩1,000,000, living with you) also makes you single-earner.

items.q: How much in assets disqualifies me?
items.a: ₩240M or more in household assets disqualifies you; ₩170M to under ₩240M halves the credit. Debts are not subtracted, and a rental deposit counts at the lower of the contract amount and the deemed deposit (55% of standard price). The reference date is June 1 of the income year.

May filing uses the full year's income and pays by the end of September. Half-year filing, for wage-only households, is filed in September and the following March; 35% of the annual amount is paid in December and the rest is settled in June. Business income rules out half-year filing.

items.q: What if I miss the deadline?
items.a: Filing within 6 months after the May window pays 95% of the amount. 2025 income can be filed until December 1, 2026, with payment within 4 months.

items.q: How much is the child tax credit?
items.a: ₩500k–₩1M per dependent child under 18. Single-earners get ₩1M per child below ₩21M of earnings and dual-earners below ₩25M, decreasing up to total income under ₩70M. Single households have no dependent children, so they do not qualify.

items.q: I got the child tax credit at year-end. Can I still get this?
items.a: Yes, but you cannot get both in full: the child tax credit you actually received is subtracted. If less than ₩30,000 remains, you get ₩30,000.
Amounts under ₩15,000 are not paid. In the low-income phase-in range ₩15,000–₩100,000 becomes ₩100,000, and in the phase-out range ₩15,000–₩30,000 becomes ₩30,000.
Use the QR code on the NTS notice, the mobile notice, ARS (1544-9944), or Hometax. Without a notice you can still apply on Hometax if you qualify. Help line: 1566-3636.

If the government's plan passes, from 2027 income the limits become ₩26M single, ₩37M single-earner and ₩52M dual-earner, and the maximums ₩1.8M, ₩3.1M and ₩3.6M. 2026 income (filed May 2027) uses the current rules.
